chunks: He gives you an example from your own life: Do you possess among your dependants any partners in what We have bestowed on you, so that you and they have equal (share) in it, and that you fear them as you fear each other? That is how We explain Our signs clearly for those who comprehend.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the analogy of slaves in Surah Ar-Rum regarding God's uniqueness?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (30:28) is often interpreted as a critique of polytheism by drawing a parallel between human social hierarchies and divine sovereignty, emphasizing that just as slaves are not equal to their masters in status or fear, created beings cannot be true partners to the Creator. The rhetorical question challenges the logical consistency of attributing shared authority to idols, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (Oneness) as a rational truth accessible to those who reflect. This analogy serves to dismantle the notion of divine multiplicity by highlighting the inherent inequality between the Creator and the created.
